Kind.Aware. Ready.
Welcome to City of London School, a leading academic day school for boys aged 10-18. We provide an education in the broadest sense, combining academic excellence with exceptional pastoral care, framed by an outward-looking and forward-thinking approach.
We are a considerate community of people who care for others as much as themselves.
We understand that for pupils to thrive they must be happy. It is why we cherish individuality, shun stereotypes, and ensure every member of our community feels included and safe to learn, so they can be the very best version of themselves. We support and help to develop the health, happiness and wellbeing of our pupils and staff, so that they can succeed at School, and beyond.
We are a diverse community who take action to help shape the world around us.
With a vibrant, multicultural city on our doorstep, we draw strength from difference, recognising that diverse perspectives can help answer big questions. As a result, staff and pupils are keenly aware of their responsibility and capacity to make a difference, right now. We are a school that fully prepares respectful, optimistic and inquisitive citizens who are politically aware and ready to play an active role in a fast-evolving society.
We are a forward-looking community prepared for a fast-changing society.
We ensure our pupils are ready for the rapidly changing demands of the coming decades, whether they relate to the job market, advances in technology or global challenges. This shows in our commitment to academic excellence, but also in our restless curiosity and desire to improve in everything we do. It means our boys are equipped to provide the kind, inquisitive and respectful leadership that our society will so urgently require in the decades ahead.
Unashamedly academic and ready for a fast-changing world
We stimulate curious minds who pursue learning for its own sake. Through robust and exceptional teaching, our pupils discover what excites and inspires them so that they can thrive in university, work and throughout life. As part of an outward-looking community of academic excellence, our pupils combine intellectual humility, critical thinking and practical wisdom to become the leaders of tomorrow, creating positive change in our fast-changing world.

Joining CLS
CLS is a happy school, enabling the development of young people who are comfortable in their own skin, empathetic and outward-looking.
Our home in the heart of London is central to that vision, giving pupils opportunities to engage directly with the world around them and making the city an extension of the classroom.
We are privileged to be in the heart of a magnificent capital City, surrounded by the country's foremost leaders and thinkers.

Academic Ethos
We are a high achieving school. Our record in examination results and entry to top universities is enviable. But we achieve this without unnecessary pressure.
The curriculum we offer is underpinned by innumerable activities and we have a strong pastoral programme which fosters resilience and independence of spirit. It is our aim to prepare our pupils for the ever changing world ahead.
We are a leading academic school with a high level of achievement, excellent examination results, and impressive progression to top universities in this country and abroad.
Encouraging excellence, achieving aspirations
Our academic ethos is rooted in our values of being Kind, Aware, and Ready. This means catering for each pupil’s individual needs through specialised learning support. Whilst we are proud of our pupils’ achievements in public exams, we also encourage learning for its own sake. We want to stimulate the desire to challenge, question and argue, so that our pupils can develop into outward-looking young adults ready for the wider world.
At City of London School, we believe that good teaching and learning develops:
Creative thought
Critical thinking and enquiry
Intellectual curiosity
Problem-solving
Research skills
Creative thought and critical thinking and enquiry.
Self-efficacy
Curating a curriculum for a changing world
Our curriculum echoes our values as a School. A strong base founded on tried and tested subject matter, but that isn’t afraid to lead the way at the cutting edge of the latest developments. Our curriculum evolves to ensure that the pupils are being taught the most up-to-date, relevant and empowering topics, with the incorporation of new subjects among the classics, including our innovative Design, Computing and Robotics course, now featuring a module on advancements in Artificial Intelligence.
Preparing for more
Consistently, we send about one fifth of our leavers to Oxbridge, a dozen to Medical School, and about a third to the top London universities (King’s, UCL, Imperial, Queen Mary, LSE). Increasingly, our pupils are also looking to other countries for their higher education; a number attend many of the global top 10 universities, including Harvard, University of California and Stanford.
Academic Opportunities
Essay Competitions
Pupils regularly excel in essay competitions such as Erasmus, John Locke, Peterhouse, Juvenes Translatores and Trinity.
Olympiad Competitions
Olympiad competitions in subjects such as Maths, Biology, Chemistry & Physics provide a national stage for pupils’ talents.
Inter-house Competitions
Inter-house competitions in disciplines such as prose and poetry encourage healthy competition.
LAMDA Qualifications
Pupils can develop confidence and presentational skills with the LAMDA qualifications (London Academy of Music & Dramatic Art).
Extended Projects
Extended Projects can compliment A-Level study and are enriched by the resources at our finger-tips in our Central London location.
IGEM Competition
Our pupils have excelled at the IGEM Competition (International Genetically Engineered Machines).
Annual Science Conference
The School hosts an annual science conference in partnership with the City of London Corporation and its academies, held at Guildhall.

The John Carpenter Alumni Community
Your relationship with CLS does not finish when you leave school.
As an Old Citizen, you are part of a supportive, engaged and interconnected network of alumni across the world.
This special community nurtures lifelong connections, inspires personal and professional growth and actively engages in the enrichment of the wider school community. It is a source of inspiration for current and future pupils.
The Philanthropy & External Engagement Team is dedicated to supporting all Old Citizens in their lifelong relationship with City of London School and each other.
Make sure you stay in touch – we can’t wait to see you.
development@cityoflondonschool..org.uk 020 3680 6314

Grow your network
Are you an Old Citizen wanting to develop your network and receive career advice? Looking for your first job or planning your next move?
Or perhaps you are an experienced professional keen to pass on your knowledge to the next generation? Whether in person at the termly networking events or online, your alumni community is here to help you.
You can use the LinkedIn ‘Alumni’ tab to find your own mentor or become one yourself.
For any alumni queries, please contact us or call 020 3680 6314.

These in depth alumni interviews give readers the chance to engage with the rich personal and professional paths experienced by Old Citizens after leaving school.

One of London's leading Independent schools
When visiting City of London School, you cannot help but sense a buzz: pupils and staff alike exude enthusiasm for the opportunities that an education here provides.
CLS is defined by its iconic location, a wonderfully diverse pupil body, outstanding pastoral care, academic excellence and an exciting co-curriculum. Our home in the heart of London is far more than an address; it is an extension of the classroom, providing daily opportunities to engage with the world’s leading cultural, legal, financial and academic institutions.
We are grounded and unpretentious, but ambitious nonetheless. And we understand that, for our pupils to make progress, they must be comfortable in their own skin.
Within this context, we are committed to preparing respectful, optimistic and inquisitive pupils for the rapidly changing demands of the twenty-first century. We understand that this requires an understanding of the society of which they are part: they must be aware. It requires a broad range of skills, academic and otherwise: they must be ready. But, most of all, it requires empathy and understanding: they must be kind.
We are proud to be a leading academic school with a high level of achievement, excellent examination results, and impressive progression to leading universities. This year, we celebrated our best ever GCSE results, and 40% of our leavers enrolling at universities ranked in the global top 10. Within the UK, we consistently send about 95% of our pupils to Russell Group (or other UK top 10) universities, with about one-fifth to Oxford and Cambridge.
Equally important is our determination to make a City of London School education available to as many boys as possible, including through means-tested support and transformational bursaries. I am proud to be the Head of a school that has this as a central priority, and we are very grateful to all who help us to make this happen.
A website can provide a flavour of the School, and I hope our Strategic Vision will provide a sense of our priorities for the coming years. However, nothing substitutes for a visit. I look forward to welcoming you to one of our regular Open Events.

A telescopic legacy

Volunteering Opportunities
Old Citizens regularly support pupils by sharing their knowledge, insight, and experiences with pupils at various stages of their time at CLS to help get them ready for life beyond school. Take a look at the opportunities below and get in touch if you’d like to get involved.
We are so grateful to have such wonderful alumni volunteers, whether they’re speaking to pupils or hosting our industry networking breakfasts, they add such value to our community.
Email chambersb@cityoflondonschoolorg.uk or the alumni team to volunteer!
What can I do to help?
Click the links below to find out how you can help. A current priority is to find support with workplace experience either virtually or in person for Summer 2026. In 2025. more than 45 organisations hosted 100 pupils and we’d love to expand those figures this year.
The Futures team can help you to develop an offering- get in touch with Employability Co-Ordinator Mousumi Chatterjee chatterjeem@cityflondonschool.org.uk to discuss.
More detail and other opportunities below
Workplace experience
Can you offer a work experience placement to a Fifth and Sixth Form pupils during their school holidays for as little as a day or longer, particularly those who may not have a personal network to draw upon. These experiences will help pupils build valuable transferable skills. We would assist you in structuring what pupils might do on the placements and any other formalities required.
Workplace encounters
Pupils seeing different work environments has a positive impact on employability skills and career decision-making, whilst providing pupils with an opportunity to learn more about the world of work. Particularly to our Fourth Form pupils (aged 14), we would be thrilled to hear from Old Citizens who would be interested in hosting CLS pupils on workplace visits.
Micro - internships
We are looking to partner with organisations across a range of sectors to create an eight-week programme for pupils to undertake work-related projects focusing on solving complex and genuine problems. These projects would begin with a workplace visit and culminate in our pupils returning to the workplace to present their work and receive feedback. Between visits, pupils would work on the projects, in teams, at school.
Examples of the skills that we seek to develop through this initiative include communication, collaboration, digital skills, problem solving and analytical skills, multidisciplinary thinking and commercial awareness.
I would like to help. Please email our Director of Futures, Bodil Chambers, to find out more.
Futures Café
Lower School pupils (aged 11-13) are just starting to learn about the range of career opportunities open to them and make links between their academic subjects and careers. Would you enjoy speaking to our Lower School pupils at our weekly Futures Café to broaden their horizons, encourage them to challenge preconceived ideas and harness their enthusiasm for career exploration.
Networking breakfasts
Supporting our Middle and Senior School pupils (aged 13-18), these sector-themed 8am networking breakfasts will enable pupils to explore career opportunities in their sector of interest in greater depth, benefitting from the experiences of those working in the sector. The breakfasts also develop pupils’ communication skills, particularly their ability to engage in professional conversations.
Career management skills workshops
Could you host workshops, primarily aimed at Sixth Formers, to help them develop important career management skills. These could take place in school, or in your workplace, and could last anything from an hour to a day. They could be aimed at a small group of pupils, or any number up to the whole year group.

Partnership
CLS has a strategic vision and commitment to working in collaboration with others and view these partnerships as critical tools for tackling disadvantage and promoting equality of opportunity, enhancing social mobility, and both cultural and social capital.
Partnership work also enables us to support social justice objectives within and beyond our wider school communities.
Partnership in Numbers
hours were invested by pupils in voluntary service across 2025
pupils from London schools visit CLS each week through partnerships
pupils in the Junior Sixth Form volunteer for mentoring schemes
The Family of Schools
As a school we place enormous value on our connections with the City of London Corporation ‘Family of Schools’ (which includes four independent schools, one maintained primary school, eight sponsored academies as part of the City of London Academies Trust, and two co-sponsored academies in neighbouring boroughs).
Partnership with this group of schools is thriving, with a wealth of opportunities for pupils and staff members to collaborate with others and bring to life our values of Kind, Aware, Ready. A defining example of this is our longstanding partnership with City of London School for Girls (CLSG), through which pupils benefit from joint academic, creative and co-curricular opportunities.
Every year we publish a Partnership Report reflecting the many ways we engage with others beyond our own community. It is a cornerstone of school life and the Reports bear testimony to the high levels of pupil engagement, be it in volunteering in the IntoUniversity Centres we support or acting as online reading mentors for primary school children. As was recognised in our most recent ISI inspection, our pupils really do demonstrate an extraordinary commitment to service, and an understanding that they can make a difference, right now.

Governors & Staff
Committed to providing an exceptional education.
Alan has been the Head at CLS since January 2018, having joined us from Brighton College where he was Deputy Head.
Alan holds an MA in Economics from the University of Cambridge and an MSc in Economics from the London School of Economics and Political Science where he was an Economic and Social Research Council scholar. Before joining Brighton College in 2010, Alan spent eight years as Head of Politics at Tonbridge School and, before that, he taught Economics at the Royal Grammar School, Guildford where he was educated as a boy.
Alan was a governor at the London Academy of Excellence, and currently serves as a governor at James Allen’s Girls’ School.
Senior Management Team
Mark is responsible for many aspects of the day-to-day running of the School. He teaches Chemistry.
Basher looks after the pastoral and academic needs of our Fourth and Fifth Form pupils. He also coordinates the DEI forums at the school. He teaches Russian and Drama and is a DDSL.
Paul looks after the pastoral concerns of the oldest pupils at our School. He teaches French and is a DDSL.
Noeleen is involved in Alumni events and has responsibility for a range of academic matters. She also organises a range of trips and all possible quiz competitions. She teaches History.
As DSL, Alice is responsible for all safeguarding matters. She oversees all matters relating to pupil welfare and pastoral care. Alice also teaches Religion and Philosophy.
Andrew coordinates all co-curricular activities from sports fixtures to educational visits. He is also responsible for 'pupil voice', leads on sustainability and is a DDSL. He teaches History.
Glenn is responsible for the School’s curriculum, pedagogical approach, teaching practice and standards, and educational innovation. He teaches Religion & Philosophy.
Patrick oversees the personal and academic development of all pupils in the Lower School and is also a deputy safeguarding lead. He teaches Innovative Design & Visual Arts.
Philip oversees the admission of new pupils to CLS. He is also responsible for the School’s internal and external communications. He teaches Geography.
Kathrin leads our marketing and communications, and works with alumni, parents, and organisations who support CLS and our bursary programme. Her team also nurtures our alumni community.
Sofie is a DDSL and manages all safeguarding cases at the school. She works closely with the other members of the Pastoral Team.
Chris is responsible for ensuring we use data and technology to support our pupils' progress in an impactful way. He teaches Economics.
Sara looks after the shared services functions of governance, operations and estates across the three City Schools. She works closely with Katie Kerr.
Katie looks after the shared service functions of HR and Finance across the three City Schools. She works closely with Sara Seymour-Savage.

Our History
CLS has a rich and proud history, dating from our inception in the 15th century through the will of John Carpenter, through to our founding on Milk Street in 1837 and our relocation to our current home in 1987. As a forward-thinking School, we nonetheless recognise the importance of where we began, and we celebrate our historical roots.
Please take a moment to read the passage on ‘The History of School’ as written by Lionel Knight MBE (Class of 1958).
Research and Enquiries
We aim to respond to all queries as promptly as we can and information is made accessible at the discretion of the London Archives, in compliance with the Data Protection Act.
Alternatively you can call us on 020 3680 6300.
Looking to Donate?
The Archive is delighted to accept items to further enrich our collections. If you have something you wish to donate please get in touch.
